lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
17 ÷ 5 = ? Explain the remainder in a sharing story and a packing story.

FEEDBACK
3 r2; sharing: 3 each, 2 left; packing full groups of 5: 4 groups needed to hold all if leftovers must be packed.

WATCH FOR
Dropping the remainder without reading the question can undercount what is needed.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Solve twelve division-with-remainder problems. For each, state quotient and remainder and write a one-line context decision for six.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

WORKED MODEL

TRY FIRST
17 ÷ 5 = ? Explain the remainder in a sharing story and a packing story.

FEEDBACK
3 r2; sharing: 3 each, 2 left; packing full groups of 5: 4 groups needed to hold all if leftovers must be packed.
teach_steps.explain:
Remainders are what is left after equal groups; context decides whether to keep the remainder, round up or ignore leftover pieces.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Dropping the remainder without reading the question can undercount what is needed. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
